newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG PM Chan refuses to resign - Australian radio.
newsitem.headline: PNG PM Chan refuses to resign - Australian radio.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said on Monday he would not resign as demanded by the country's defence chief, Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio reported.

The ABC also reported from Port Moresby that the country's police chief, earlier reported to be supporting the defence force commander, had rejected the army's ultimatum and was backing the prime minister and his government.

Papua New Guinea's army chief Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok earlier said he had the backing of the police in his demand that Chan resign for hiring mercenaries to end the secessionist conflict on Bougainville island.
Singirok said he was not staging a coup.

"Chan says he has received a letter (from the defence chief) and will not resign," said an ABC reporter in Port Moresby. The reporter said he had spoken to the PNG police commissioner who said he backed the Chan government not the army.
Papua New Guinea has engaged 40 African mercenaries to train government troops for a mission on Bougainville, where the PNG army has been unsuccessful against a nine-year uprising.
